title: Day 722 — Sheinbaum Rebuts Trump's 'Epicenter' Remarks, Reports 5 Drones Downed at Border, Urges INE to Regulate Social-Media Algorithms
detail: At her September 23, 2026 (Day 722, Wednesday) mañanera in the National Palace, President Sheinbaum responded to President Trump's UN General Assembly remarks calling Mexico the "epicenter" of cartel violence, saying media coverage selectively quoted him while omitting his acknowledgment of Mexico's cooperation, and reiterating "tenemos buena relación con el presidente Trump." She noted she could just as easily point to the difficulty of neighboring a country with high illegal drug consumption and domestic gun manufacturing but chooses not to escalate, citing continued coordination under the binational Operación Águila and observing that "tienen elecciones en noviembre y Trump usa a México en las campañas." She reported that five unauthorized commercial drones were disabled inside Mexican territory near the US border, saying binational security collaboration must rest on mutual respect. Separately, she proposed the INE study minimum regulation of social-media algorithms, paid political advertising, automated ('bot') accounts and AI-generated content ahead of the 2027 midterms, noting 94.5% of Mexicans get news and information through social platforms and citing manipulation risks like those alleged in Colombia's elections. She also disputed international 'forced disappearance' framing, saying most of the roughly 30,000 open missing-persons cases involve people who left voluntarily rather than state-ordered disappearances; confirmed she is skipping the UN General Assembly in person for a second consecutive year, sending Foreign Secretary Roberto Velasco while she plans to attend APEC in China in November; and voiced support for Brazil's Lula da Silva against Washington pressure while reiterating opposition to trade blockades and foreign electoral interference regarding Venezuela, Cuba, Iran and Palestine.

media.caption: Sheinbaum responds to Trump's UN 'epicenter' remarks and calls for INE regulation of social-media algorithms
Sheinbaum's September 23 mañanera addresses border drones and Trump's UN remarks

title: Day 722 — Sheinbaum Details 2,400km Passenger-Rail Buildout: AIFA-Pachuca 45%, CDMX-Querétaro 31%, 750 Billion Pesos Committed
detail: Sheinbaum used her September 23, 2026 mañanera to detail progress on the government's 2,400km national passenger-rail program, backed by roughly 750 billion pesos ('750 mil mdp') in combined passenger and freight investment. She presented completion figures for four routes under construction: Mexico City (AIFA)–Pachuca Interoceánico at 45% (58km of double electrified track, 4 stations, 2 substations, 1 maintenance base, 10 work fronts, 8,800 workers of whom 21% are women), Mexico City–Querétaro at 31%, Querétaro–Irapuato at 22%, and Saltillo–Nuevo Laredo at 10%, alongside the Tren Maya cargo line at 67%. She said the AIFA-Pachuca and Mexico City-Querétaro lines are expected to begin operations in 2027, that construction has generated roughly 60,000 direct and 120,000 indirect jobs, and that the completed network will serve about 41.3 million people with average travel-time reductions near 40% and pollutant-emission cuts of up to 50%; 64 families have been relocated for right-of-way at a cost of 63.5 million pesos, with resettlement compensation ongoing. She framed the buildout — which her government says adds 40% more track than was built during the AMLO administration — as core to the nearshoring and public-investment agenda. Separately, INEGI figures presented the same day showed national population growth slowing to 0.7%, which Sheinbaum attributed to smaller family sizes and rising childlessness rather than a policy failure.

media.caption: Sheinbaum details 2,400km passenger-rail buildout progress, including the AIFA-Pachuca and CDMX-Querétaro lines
Sheinbaum's September 23 mañanera covers new train lines, population data and the response to Trump
